results.summary: This project implements three current-switching DACs designed to generate analog VGA display signals. It uses a 16x16 matrix of unit current sources, controlled by digital inputs, to produce inverted analog current outputs. The design includes a digital controller hardened with OpenLane 2 and can generate various test patterns. External hardware like a VGA display and opamp circuits are needed for full functionality, and the TinyVGA PMOD can be used for basic RGB222 output.

This chip is an automatic pump-out controller designed to manage liquid pumps based on a 60 Hz RMS current measurement. It turns on the pump, monitors for tank emptying via current drop, or stops after a timeout, with status LEDs and a button for manual operation. The design includes a development board for bring-up and validation, and testing involved RTL simulation, GL testing, and FPGA emulation.

This project implements a USB to UART bridge using the CDC (Communications Device Class) protocol. It operates at a fixed baud rate of 115200 and requires specific external resistors for USB connection. The device enumerates as a serial port on a computer, and silicon testing confirmed proper enumeration and loopback functionality. It is designed to interface with standard USB ports.

This project is a basic UART template designed to be hooked up to an Arduino. It provides the fundamental structure for a UART interface, likely intended for educational purposes or as a starting point for more complex designs. Testing involves using an Arduino to interact with the module. The documentation is minimal, stating its purpose and how to test it with external hardware.

This design implements a customizable digital padlock that can be configured with a specific code. Users can set the code using input switches and then attempt to unlock it by entering the code via a push button, with the status displayed on a seven-segment display. The design is implemented in Wokwi and requires no external hardware beyond the simulation environment. Testing involves setting the code and then attempting to unlock it.

This project implements a reverse 8-bit counter with a reset function. It is described as a dividing counter using a series of D-flip-flops, operating at a 10 Hz clock speed. Testing involves using a reset button and a step button to observe the counter's behavior. The design is implemented in Wokwi and requires LEDs connected to the output pins for visualization.

This project is a hardware implementation of a 32-bit Fibonacci linear feedback shift register (LFSR) with taps at specific registers. It includes logic to prevent the LFSR from entering an all-zero state, ensuring a maximum cycle length. The design is implemented in Wokwi and allows for manual initialization and input selection. Testing involves observing the output sequence, particularly from an all-zero state, and comparing it against expected values or a Python simulation.

This project implements a 4-bit multiplier using Verilog. The design splits the inputs into two portions, 'q' and 'm', and uses full adders to compute the product 'p'. The documentation is brief, stating the purpose and the use of full adders. Testing is performed using an 'idle' testbench to verify cases. No external hardware is required for its operation.

This project is a 3-bit, 8-channel PWM driver implemented in Verilog. It uses a 3-bit counter to generate PWM signals, with each channel's level controlled by a dedicated 3-bit register. The PWM levels range from always off (0) to always on (7). Testing involves using reset, set, address, and level pins to configure the PWM output on each channel. The design operates on a 1000 Hz clock.

This project is designed to test the proper tech-mapping of P and N latches. It provides separate P and N latch structures, each with enable and data inputs and a quality output. The P latch passes data when enabled high, while the N latch passes data when enabled low. Silicon test reports confirm that both latches function as expected, mirroring input data when enabled and holding their state otherwise.
